confidence_notes: Restaurant and coffee anchors rest on aggregated crowdsourced cost-of-living figures from 2026 and older pages, so they are moderate quality. Beer and cappuccino are the best-supported. Inexpensive and mid-range meal anchors vary widely by source, so they are bounded estimates. Cocktail is a bar-tier range from one 2026 guide. Wine_glass has no direct local source; it is estimated from the beer anchor, roughly 1.5x beer, which is a model assumption. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and regional context; no booking pages or current listings were inspected. July is peak season and the August festival period can push hotel rates up, so these anchors may understate peak-week prices. FX: the 2026-11-18 value of 0.6720 was taken from a secondary site (ozfinancehub.com.au) that states it reflects RBA data. I did not open rba.gov.au and could not confirm the figure on the RBA page, so the source_url is the official RBA exchange-rates page as a reference, not a page I read.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on aggregated 2026 cost-of-living figures for Cluj-Napoca and Romanian national price levels (Cluj reported as about 22 percent above the national average, with restaurants about 23 percent above), benchmarked against mid-sized Central and Eastern European cities with comparable tourism demand. Accommodation is a holistic regional estimate.
